title: Matsya Avatar: The Fish Who Saved the World
sources: Bhagavata Purana, Canto 8, chapter 24 (King Satyavrata, the Kritamala river, the growing fish, the seven-day warning, the boat tied to the horn with Vasuki, Hayagriva and the Vedas)
Matsya Purana, chapters 1-2, and Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1 (Manu and the fish, the earliest version of the flood story)

lines.text: Long ago, a gentle king named Satyavrata
lines.say: Long ago, a gentle king named Suttya-vrutta

lines.text: knelt by a river to offer water in prayer.
A tiny fish shimmered in his cupped hands,
and whispered, please, protect me.
So the king carried it home in a water pot.
lines.caps: SO THE *KING | CARRIED IT *HOME | IN A *WATER POT

lines.text: But by morning, the fish had outgrown it.
lines.caps: BUT BY *MORNING | THE FISH HAD *OUTGROWN IT

lines.text: He moved it to a pond,
then a lake,
then a mighty river,
until even the ocean could barely hold it.
The king bowed and asked, who are you, really?
The golden fish replied, I am Vishnu, protector of the worlds.
lines.caps: THE *GOLDEN FISH | I AM *VISHNU | *PROTECTOR | OF THE *WORLDS

lines.text: In seven days, a great flood will swallow the earth.
lines.caps: IN *SEVEN DAYS | A GREAT *FLOOD | WILL *SWALLOW | THE *EARTH

lines.text: Gather the seven sages, the seeds of every plant,
lines.caps: GATHER THE | *SEVEN SAGES | THE *SEEDS | OF EVERY *PLANT

lines.text: and every creature, and wait for me.
Meanwhile, a demon named Hayagriva stole the sacred Vedas,
lines.say: Meanwhile, a demon named Hie-uh-greeva stole the sacred Vaydas,

lines.text: and hid them deep beneath the sea.
On the seventh day, the skies broke open,
and the oceans rose above the mountains.
Just then, a shining boat appeared, and so did Matsya,
lines.caps: JUST *THEN | A *SHINING BOAT | AND SO DID *MATSYA
lines.say: Just then, a shining boat appeared, and so did Mutsya,

lines.text: now vast as a mountain, with one golden horn.
Using the serpent Vasuki as a rope,
lines.say: Using the serpent Vah-sookee as a rope,

lines.text: the king tied the boat to that horn.
All through the stormy night, Matsya pulled them across the waves.
lines.caps: THE *STORMY NIGHT | MATSYA *PULLED THEM | ACROSS THE *WAVES
lines.say: All through the stormy night, Mutsya pulled them across the waves.

lines.text: Then he dove into the deep, defeated the demon,
and carried the Vedas back into the light.
lines.say: and carried the Vaydas back into the light.

lines.text: When the waters settled, a new dawn rose,
and life began again.
This is Matsya, the first avatar of Vishnu,
lines.say: This is Mutsya, the first avatar of Vishnu,

lines.text: a reminder that one small act of kindness can save the world.
lines.caps: A *REMINDER | ONE *SMALL ACT | OF *KINDNESS | CAN *SAVE | THE *WORLD
